channel.title: Github on Sujith Quintelier
channel.description: Recent content in Github on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — August 31
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s latest weekly release adds more model choice and content protection controls. VS Code also gets new options for managing agent sessions and preparing pull requests for merge.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GPT-6 Astra is generally available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GPT-6 Astra from OpenAI is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. GitHub says the model is intended for long-horizon, autonomous coding and agentic tasks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: New API endpoint provides privacy-safe star history data
item.description:
GitHub added a new REST API endpoint for repository star history that lets users track star growth over time without exposing individual stargazer identities. This follows earlier restrictions on stargazer listing endpoints to admins and collaborators.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Multiple trusted publishing configurations for npm
item.description:
GitHub says three npm publishing updates are now generally available, including support for multiple trusted publishing configurations per package. The post also mentions staged publishing and another publishing-related change, but the provided excerpt does not include the full details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Actions: Early September 2026 updates
item.description:
GitHub Actions added three updates focused on workflow visibility and control. The post highlights a new REST API for runner version deprecations, but the provided excerpt does not include the full details of the other changes.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Upcoming deprecation of selected GitHub Copilot models
item.description:
GitHub will deprecate selected Copilot models across all Copilot experiences on October 2, 2026. The affected models include Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub CLI Linux package signing key expires September 5
item.description:
The GitHub CLI Linux package repository signing key expires on September 5, 2026. After that date, repository metadata in APT and RPM workflows will be affected starting with the first release published after expiration.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Gemini 3.8 Flash is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now supports Gemini 3.8 Flash, Google’s latest Flash model. GitHub says early testing showed strong performance on complex terminal-based coding tasks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Reopening Copilot Business and Enterprise signups
item.description:
GitHub is gradually reopening sign-ups for Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise for customers paying by credit card or PayPal over the next few weeks. Availability is rolling out gradually to people who have been waiting to start.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.26.4 improves GitHub actions security detections
item.description:
CodeQL 2.26.4 is a new release that adds support for Go 1.27 and improves GitHub Actions security detections. It is part of the static analysis engine used by GitHub code scanning.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise-managed settings support any default model
item.description:
Enterprise-managed settings can now set any supported GitHub Copilot model as the default for new conversations. This lets enterprises choose the default model that best matches their workflow.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Content exclusions generally available in Copilot app and CLI
item.description:
GitHub Copilot app and CLI now honor content exclusion policies set at the enterprise, organization, and repository levels. Excluded files will not be used as context by Copilot.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise Live Migrations from GHES to ghe.com generally available
item.description:
Enterprise Live Migrations is now generally available for near-zero-downtime repository migrations from GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) to GitHub Enterprise Cloud with Data Residency (GHEC DR).

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Set an expiration date for individual user budgets
item.description:
GitHub now lets you set an optional expiration date on an individual user budget. When the date is reached, GitHub automatically removes the budget; the feature is generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review can now approve pull requests
item.description:
Copilot code review can now indicate when a pull request is ready for approval, and repository admins can authorize it to approve the PR. The approval capability is disabled by default.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Block users from discussion comments in personal repositories
item.description:
GitHub added in-context blocking controls for discussion comments in repositories owned by personal accounts. Users can now block or unblock other users directly from discussion comments, matching the existing issue and pull request comment behavior.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Claude Fable 5.1 is generally available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Claude Fable 5.1 from Anthropic is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. GitHub says it is intended for long-horizon, autonomous coding and knowledge-work tasks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub CLI: Media in issues, pull requests, and comments
item.description:
GitHub CLI now supports a repeatable --attach flag to upload local images or videos and insert them inline in issue, pull request, or comment bodies. This adds media attachment support to GitHub CLI posts and comments.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot model access update for GitHub Team plans
item.description:
GitHub updated how Copilot model access is determined for users with seats in more than one organization. The change is intended to keep billing and governance aligned.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Selected GitHub Copilot models deprecated
item.description:
GitHub has deprecated selected Copilot models across most Copilot experiences, including Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions, effective September 1, 2026. The post notes that the affected models are no longer available in those experiences.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in VS Code, August 2026 releases
item.description:
VS Code v1.132 through v1.135, released in August 2026, add improvements to GitHub Copilot workflows focused on organizing agent sessions, reviewing changes, and navigating longer conversations. The changelog also mentions updates to Agent Host, but the provided excerpt does not include the details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio — August update
item.description:
GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio’s August 2026 update adds more control over Copilot reasoning, model selection, sharing specialized agents within teams, and timing code review requests. The post is a high-level changelog summary rather than a detailed feature list.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — August 24
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s August 24 weekly release notes highlight more control over Copilot behavior across Slack, Teams, the app, CLI, and IDEs. The post mentions team sessions in Slack and Teams plus broader customization options, but the provided excerpt does not include specific feature details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Upcoming changes to GitHub Copilot policies and billing
item.description:
GitHub says three upcoming changes are coming to Copilot policies and billing. The post is a notice to review the updates, but the provided excerpt does not include the actual policy or billing details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Better label management on issues is generally available
item.description:
GitHub says improved label management for issues is now generally available. The update is aimed at making labels easier to organize and find in repositories with large or growing label lists.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review: Resolution reasons and expanded capabilities
item.description:
Copilot code review now supports two additional pull request types: PRs authored by bots (including Copilot cloud agent) and very large pull requests. GitHub also added resolution reasons for code review outcomes.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Classroom deprecated
item.description:
GitHub Classroom was deprecated on August 28, 2026 and replaced by selected partner solutions. The Classroom website, APIs, and related services have been decommissioned.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Actions retention will cover checks, workflow runs, and statuses
item.description:
Starting October 1, 2026, GitHub Actions retention settings will also apply to checks, workflow runs, and statuses, in addition to artifacts and logs. These data types will follow the same retention policy going forward.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Close all open contributions authored by a blocked user
item.description:
GitHub added an option to automatically close all open issues, discussions, and pull requests from a user when you block them from a personal account or organization. This applies to contributions authored by the blocked user at the time the block is set.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise-managed settings now support autoUpdate for plugin marketplaces
item.description:
Enterprise-managed settings now let admins enable automatic updates for specific plugin marketplaces by setting autoUpdate: true on an extraKnownMarketplaces entry. Supported clients will check the marketplace and update it automatically.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Global model policy generally available
item.description:
GitHub is gradually rolling out enforcement of a default global model policy for generally available GitHub Copilot models on Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise plans. The policy was announced in July and is now generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Apps can now access enterprise billing data
item.description:
GitHub Apps can now be granted access to enterprise billing data by enterprise owners. The app configuration flow now includes an enterprise billing permission that can be selected when creating or updating an app.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Rule insights dashboard generally available
item.description:
The rule insights dashboard is now generally available for both repositories and organizations. It provides a visual, high-level view of how GitHub evaluates and enforces repository rules.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot app Customize tab is generally available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s new Customize tab in the Copilot app is now generally available. It is meant to connect Copilot with a team’s existing tools, knowledge, and workflows, including MCP.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Block users directly from security advisories
item.description:
GitHub now lets repository owners block a user directly from a security advisory page in public repositories. The feature is available for repositories owned by organizations or personal accounts.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Push rules in rulesets now support path exceptions
item.description:
Push rules in GitHub rulesets now support path exceptions, letting you exempt specific file paths so a rule applies everywhere else in scope. The feature is available in public preview.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Better tools for managing blocked users
item.description:
GitHub updated blocked-user management for personal accounts and organizations. The blocked users list now supports search, sorting, and pagination to make large lists easier to manage.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: The new GitHub Copilot experience in Slack
item.description:
GitHub’s Slack integration now includes agentic GitHub Copilot capabilities from Copilot CLI and the Copilot app, available in public preview. Users can interact with @GitHub in Slack to work with these features.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Shared agentic work with GitHub Copilot in Microsoft Teams
item.description:
GitHub Copilot can now be started from Microsoft Teams by mentioning @GitHub in a channel, thread, or direct message. This creates a shared agent session that participants can view and help guide.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Pinning saved views to the repository issues sidebar is generally available and more
item.description:
GitHub now lets you pin saved views to a repository’s issues sidebar, so frequently used views are easier to access. The feature is generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Windows 11 arm64 VS2026 image generally available
item.description:
Windows 11 arm64 images with Visual Studio 2026 are now generally available on standard and larger GitHub-hosted runners. Workflows can use the new image by updating the runner image reference.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Code scanning adds a mitigated alert dismissal reason
item.description:
Code scanning now supports dismissing alerts with the reason “Mitigated” when the vulnerability still exists in code but is offset by external controls, such as a web application firewall or network protections.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Separate GitHub Actions path for GitHub Code Quality
item.description:
GitHub Code Quality CodeQL Actions workflows now have a dedicated workflow path and are generally available. Run history and Actions usage reports can now distinguish GitHub Code Quality runs from other Actions workflows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Track GitHub Code Quality enablement changes in the audit log
item.description:
GitHub Code Quality now emits audit log events when it is enabled, disabled, or its repository settings are changed. This adds a history trail for Code Quality configuration changes.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.26.3 improves GitHub Actions queries and JavaScript modeling
item.description:
CodeQL 2.26.3 adds source modeling for JavaScript, TypeScript, and Vue, and updates several GitHub Actions queries for better accuracy. It is a CodeQL release used by GitHub code scanning.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Track organization code quality trends
item.description:
GitHub’s organization-level Code Quality dashboard now has a Trends tab. It shows code quality changes across repositories over time instead of only a point-in-time view.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise managed settings in GitHub Copilot for JetBrains
item.description:
GitHub Copilot for JetBrains now supports enterprise managed settings. Administrators can centrally control plugin governance, MCP server access, OpenTelemetry, and permission modes across the enterprise.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Credential revocation and deauthorization by token type
item.description:
GitHub added self-service incident response actions to deauthorize and revoke user credentials by token type and by specific user. The update extends existing credential revocation workflows for security incidents.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Multiple redirect URIs and token refresh for OAuth apps
item.description:
GitHub updated OAuth app and GitHub App platform support to improve app security. The changes include optional expiring access tokens with refresh tokens for OAuth apps, and support for multiple redirect URIs.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Grok 4.6 is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Grok 4.6 is now rolling out in GitHub Copilot as a new reasoning model from xAI. GitHub says it is intended for agentic coding and complex multi-step workflows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — August 10
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s August 10 weekly release adds new models, portable plugins, and workflow improvements for agents. The updates are aimed at making Copilot more flexible across editors, the command line, and the Copilot app.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: License data quality improvements
item.description:
GitHub now sources license information for dependency graph software components from package registries such as npmjs.org and PyPI. This is intended to improve the accuracy and completeness of displayed license data.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Block users from comments in personal repositories
item.description:
GitHub now lets you block or unblock users directly from comments on pull requests and issues in repositories owned by personal accounts. The action can be performed from the comment interface.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Gemini 3.7 Flash is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GitHub Copilot is rolling out Gemini 3.7 Flash, Google’s latest Flash model. GitHub says early testing showed improvements in web and app development and agentic tasks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Agent Plugins 1.0 in VS Code, Copilot CLI, and the Copilot app
item.description:
GitHub published Agent Plugins 1.0, enabling a plugin to be built once and used across compatible agent clients. The release is available in VS Code, Copilot CLI, and the Copilot app, with support announced alongside AWS, Anysphere, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Vercel.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Rule insights for organizations in public preview
item.description:
GitHub has released the rule insights dashboard in public preview for organizations. It provides a visual overview of how repository rulesets are evaluated and enforced at the organization level.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Enterprise Server 3.22 release candidate
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Server 3.22 release candidate is now available. The post says it introduces new platform capabilities, with one highlighted change being administrator configuration for Copilot CLI.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot memory and Ollama in GitHub Copilot for JetBrains
item.description:
GitHub Copilot for JetBrains adds persistent memory, local model access via Ollama, and additional enterprise controls. The update also improves chat workflows and fixes reliability issues with MCP servers.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Automatically migrate branch protection rules to repository rulesets
item.description:
GitHub now lets you convert existing branch protection rules into repository rulesets from repository settings. This provides a direct migration path to the newer policy framework.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Upcoming deprecation of MAI-Code-1-Flash
item.description:
GitHub will deprecate MAI-Code-1-Flash across all GitHub Copilot experiences on September 10, 2026. The suggested replacement is MAI-Code-1.1-Flash.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: MAI-Code-1.1-Flash available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
MAI-Code-1.1-Flash is rolling out in GitHub Copilot. It adds native vision support for image understanding and improves coding quality over MAI-Code-1-Flash.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Per-model token breakdown in the usage report
item.description:
GitHub’s usage report now includes a per-model breakdown of tokens behind AI credits. The report shows token details for each model, including input, output, and cache usage.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot on web expands conversation controls
item.description:
GitHub updated Copilot Chat on github.com with new conversation controls to make the web experience easier to use. The changes include quicker access to recent chats and the ability to minimize the chat panel.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub billing in India now supports automatic recurring payments
item.description:
GitHub billing in India now supports automatic recurring payments for monthly and annual bills when using eligible saved credit cards. The change uses a payment mandate for recurring charges.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Custom thread subscriptions are being deprecated
item.description:
GitHub is deprecating custom thread subscription settings for notifications. Users will no longer be able to configure them, and support for existing custom thread subscription settings will be removed.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — August 3
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s August 3 weekly release notes mention updates across the desktop app, CLI, and VS Code focused on resuming and organizing work, reviewing changes, and asking questions without losing context. The provided excerpt does not include the specific feature details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprises can now install third-party GitHub Apps
item.description:
Enterprise owners can now install public GitHub Apps built outside their enterprise on enterprise accounts. This enables third-party integrations for enterprise management scenarios.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot impact dashboard adds a return on investment section
item.description:
The Copilot impact dashboard now includes a “Potential return on investment” section. It links Copilot spend to pull request output to help estimate ROI.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review effort levels are generally available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot code review effort levels are now generally available. Lite and Balanced let you choose review depth based on the complexity and risk of the code change.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot usage metrics API adds agent app activity
item.description:
The Copilot usage metrics API now includes activity from agent apps used in GitHub workflows. This extends usage reporting to agents from partners such as Claude and Codex.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: “Relates to” issue relationship in public preview and multi-select fields is generally available
item.description:
GitHub added a new public preview issue relationship called “Relates to” for connecting related work, and multi-select fields are now generally available for GitHub Projects.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Secret scanning coverage updates
item.description:
GitHub updated secret scanning coverage by adding more secrets to push protection, onboarding a new secret scanning partner, and including richer metadata in alerts. The post also notes the Secret Scanning Partnership Program now includes Lovable Labs.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Code Quality no longer adds Copilot as a reviewer
item.description:
Enabling GitHub Code Quality on a repository no longer creates a ruleset that automatically requests GitHub Copilot as a reviewer on pull requests. Existing repositories with that ruleset are affected only if they already have it configured.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: MCP allowlists in enterprise managed settings
item.description:
GitHub added enterprise-managed settings to centrally control which MCP servers GitHub Copilot clients can run. Enterprise owners can now use allowedMcpServers and deniedMcpServers to allowlist or block specific MCP servers.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Set pull request limits at the organization level
item.description:
GitHub now supports setting pull request limits at the organization level. These limits control how many open pull requests a user without write access can have.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Kimi K3 is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GitHub has resumed rolling out Kimi K3 in GitHub Copilot. The model is billed at provider list pricing under usage-based billing.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Customize code scanning default setup at scale
item.description:
GitHub added a new repository property, github-codeql-config-file, that lets you apply a custom configuration file to code scanning default setup. This gives you control over how CodeQL runs on repositories at scale.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Retiring the Copilot Billing Preview app
item.description:
GitHub has retired the Copilot Billing Preview app and it is no longer available. Copilot spend can now be reviewed and managed directly in GitHub billing settings.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Upcoming deprecation of GitHub Spark on github.com
item.description:
GitHub Spark will stop accepting new users and new app creation starting August 4, 2026. Existing users can keep using Spark until August 31, 2026.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Customize Dependabot pull request branch names
item.description:
Dependabot now supports custom pull request branch names through new pull-request-branch-name settings in .github/dependabot.yml. You can configure a prefix, maximum length, and separators for segments and words.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Code coverage automatic enablement in Code Quality settings
item.description:
GitHub added a new Code Quality setting that can automatically generate a code coverage workflow with AI. The change is meant to reduce setup time for coverage in repositories.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.26.2 adds Swift 6.3.3 and Kotlin 2.4.10 support
item.description:
CodeQL 2.26.2 has been released with support for Swift 6.3.3 and Kotlin 2.4.10. It is the static analysis engine used by GitHub code scanning.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Customize the reasoning level for Copilot cloud agent
item.description:
GitHub Copilot cloud agent now lets you set the reasoning level for supported models when delegating a task. This gives you control over how much reasoning the agent uses for a request.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise team specialization for managed settings
item.description:
Enterprise administrators can now apply managed settings using itemized configuration files targeted at enterprise teams. This lets large organizations delegate more specific governance without routing every change through central admins or relying on a single global configuration.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Trigger Copilot automations with comments
item.description:
GitHub now supports triggering Copilot cloud agent automations from new issue comments and pull request comments. This enables comment-based workflows such as generating documentation.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Triage role can bypass issue creation restrictions
item.description:
GitHub changed issue creation restrictions so users with the triage role can now create issues in repositories where issue creation is limited to collaborators only. Previously, only users with write access could create issues under that setting.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Migrate from GitLab to GitHub with GitHub Enterprise Importer
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Importer now generally supports self-serve migrations from gitlab.com and GitLab Self-Managed to GitHub Enterprise Cloud. The feature is available through GEI and the GitHub CLI.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Upcoming August 2026 model deprecations in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GitHub Copilot will deprecate several models across all Copilot experiences on September 1, 2026. The affected experiences include Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemini 3 Flash deprecated
item.description:
GitHub has deprecated Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemini 3 Flash across all Copilot experiences as of July 31, 2026. This includes Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise teams model policy targeting in public preview
item.description:
GitHub has added user-based model policy targeting for enterprise teams in public preview. It is available to GitHub Enterprise customers with Copilot Business or Copilot Enterprise licenses and lets AI administrators set a baseline policy.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Restricting npm bypass-2FA granular access tokens
item.description:
npm granular access tokens configured to bypass 2FA can no longer be used for sensitive account, organization, and package management actions. Those operations now require an interactive 2FA challenge.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Models is now retired
item.description:
GitHub Models was retired on July 30, 2026. The playground, model catalog, inference API, and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) access are no longer available to customers.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Reference same-repository actions with self-repository syntax
item.description:
GitHub added a new self-repository syntax for uses: so actions and reusable workflows in the same repository can be referenced with a $/-prefixed value. This changes how same-repo workflows/actions are addressed, but the provided text does not include further details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Stacked pull requests are now in public preview
item.description:
GitHub has put stacked pull requests into public preview. The feature lets users split a larger change into an ordered series of smaller, reviewable pull requests.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio — July update
item.description:
GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio’s July 2026 update adds a new agent built on the Copilot SDK, plus built-in expertise from the .NET and Azure teams. It also adds more options to tailor Copilot to individual workflows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Limit remote control to managed devices
item.description:
Enterprises and organizations can now limit Copilot remote control sessions to managed devices. This adds administrator control over which devices are eligible to host remote control access.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio Code, July 2026 releases
item.description:
GitHub’s July 2026 Copilot-in-VS Code changelog covers VS Code v1.127 through v1.131. The releases focus on agent workflows, reviewing changes, chat, and navigation improvements.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review: Agent skills and MCP now generally available
item.description:
Copilot code review now generally supports agent skills and MCP servers for all Copilot Pro, Pro+, Business, and Enterprise users. These features have moved from public preview to general availability.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Default model enablement for Copilot Business and Enterprise
item.description:
GitHub is introducing a global default enablement policy for generally available Copilot models on Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise plans. New GA models will be enabled by default instead of requiring admins to turn each one on manually.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.26.1 improves analysis accuracy and framework coverage
item.description:
CodeQL 2.26.1 has been released with improvements to analysis accuracy and broader framework coverage, including Go. The changelog item is brief and does not list additional specific fixes or language/framework details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot app usage metrics now expand across report rollups
item.description:
GitHub Copilot app usage metrics are now included in more of the Copilot usage metrics API. Individual app activity is now attributed to users in the enterprise-user and organization-user reports.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: npm publish-time malware scanning and dual-use metadata
item.description:
npm is adding automatic malware scanning when packages are published, along with a new metadata requirement for packages that may be used for both benign and malicious purposes. The changelog says this is part of ongoing supply-chain security work and explains what publishers should expect.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Grok 4.5 is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Grok 4.5 is now rolling out in GitHub Copilot. GitHub says the xAI model is intended for fast, agentic coding and complex multi-step workflows, with a large context window.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Dependabot alerts on malicious packages across more ecosystems
item.description:
GitHub Advisory Database now ingests malware advisories from OpenSSF’s malicious-packages repository, expanding the malware data available to Dependabot alerts. This broadens coverage across more ecosystems.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Actions holds potentially malicious workflows for approval
item.description:
GitHub Actions now detects potentially malicious workflow changes in public repositories and requires approval before they run. The change is intended to reduce supply-chain abuse from compromised credentials used to add workflows that steal CI/CD secrets or perform follow-on attacks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot for JetBrains adds improved OpenTelemetry configuration and model management
item.description:
GitHub Copilot for JetBrains now includes improved OpenTelemetry configuration and model management. The update also adds support for connecting MCP servers and custom agents in Claude agent flows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Manage GitHub Copilot app access with a dedicated policy
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now has a dedicated policy for controlling app access at both the enterprise and organization levels. This separates Copilot app access from the previous broader access controls.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise managed settings in the GitHub Copilot app and Copilot cloud agent
item.description:
GitHub Copilot app and Copilot cloud agent now support enterprise managed settings, letting organizations apply the same centrally managed Copilot policies across the enterprise.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Claude Opus 5 is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now supports Claude Opus 5, Anthropic’s latest Opus model. GitHub says it is intended for complex, long-running coding tasks that need careful reasoning and tool use.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot cloud agent for Linear is now generally available
item.description:
GitHub says Copilot cloud agent is now generally available for Linear. Users can assign Linear issues to the agent, which then analyzes the issue contents and works asynchronously in the background.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub MCP Server supports the next MCP specification
item.description:
GitHub MCP Server will support the upcoming MCP spec ahead of its official release. The key protocol change is a move to a stateless core on 28 July 2026.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Mobile: Fix failing Actions checks with Copilot cloud agent
item.description:
GitHub Mobile now lets you ask Copilot coding agent to investigate and fix failing GitHub Actions checks on a pull request directly from the mobile app. The feature starts from a failed check and uses Copilot cloud agent to work on the issue.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Limit open pull requests for users without write access
item.description:
GitHub is adding a limit on how many open pull requests users without write access can have in a repository. The change is intended to reduce repeated low-quality or drive-by PRs and ease triage load for maintainers.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Agent finder for GitHub Copilot now available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now includes agent finder, a feature for selecting which MCP servers, skills, canvases, agents, and tools an agent should use. GitHub says it reduces the need to manually wire these components and helps avoid filling the context window.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot individual plan sign-ups are reopening
item.description:
GitHub is gradually reopening sign-ups for Copilot Individual plans, including Student, Pro, Pro+, and Max, for new subscribers over the next couple of weeks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot app generally available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot app is now generally available on macOS, Windows, and Linux. It serves as a native desktop app for agent-driven development on GitHub.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Models is no longer available to new customers
item.description:
GitHub is retiring GitHub Models. As an initial step, new customers can no longer use it, while existing organizations or enterprises that have already used it are not affected by this announcement.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Code Quality generally available July 20, 2026
item.description:
GitHub Code Quality, currently in public preview, will reach general availability on July 20, 2026. The preview has been used by enterprises to detect maintainability and reliability issues, enforce quality gates, and track code coverage.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Organization-level enablement for GitHub Code Quality
item.description:
GitHub Code Quality can now be enabled or disabled at the organization level with one toggle. This replaces the need to configure the feature repository by repository.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot usage metrics now include more of your active users
item.description:
GitHub Copilot usage metrics now use server-side telemetry in addition to client-side signals, so reports include more active users. The change affects enterprise usage reports and improves coverage of user activity.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review: New configurations and controls
item.description:
GitHub added new ways to configure Copilot code review, including organization runner controls, support for Copilot content exclusion, and removal of the repository custom instructions character limit.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Actions: Minimum version enforcement timeline for self-hosted runners
item.description:
GitHub Actions is resuming enforcement of minimum version requirements for self-hosted runners on github.com and GitHub Enterprise Cloud with Data Residency. The post says this is part of a broader effort to rebuild enforcement, but the excerpt does not include the specific minimum versions or timeline details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Enterprise Server 3.21 is now generally available
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Server 3.21 is now generally available. The release adds improvements in deployment efficiency, monitoring, code security, and policy management, including organization custom properties now generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Bot-created pull requests can run workflows if approved
item.description:
Pull requests created by github-actions[bot] can now run CI/CD workflows after a user approves them. The approval step is required as a security check before generated code is allowed to trigger workflows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: AI usage report updates
item.description:
AI usage reports now include GitHub AI Credits usage in the standard report fields. To track AI credit consumption, use the quantity field for AI credit quantity and gross_amount for the associated amount.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot CLI: Configure everything from one place with /settings
item.description:
GitHub Copilot CLI adds a unified /settings command for managing configuration in one place. It consolidates older commands like /theme, /streamer-mode, and /experimental, along with other previously separate options.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: New runner images in public preview
item.description:
GitHub has added two new GitHub-hosted runner images for Actions in public preview. They are available to all users so workflows can be tested on the latest platforms before general release.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Agentic Workflows is now in public preview
item.description:
GitHub Agentic Workflows is now in public preview. It lets you automate reasoning-based tasks such as issue triage, CI failure analysis, and documentation updates using coding agents inside GitHub.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Agentic workflows no longer need a personal access token
item.description:
GitHub Agentic Workflows can now use the built-in GitHub Actions GITHUB_TOKEN instead of requiring a personal access token. This removes the need to create and store a PAT for these workflows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: List, view, and create discussions in GitHub CLI
item.description:
GitHub CLI now includes a new gh discussion command group for GitHub Discussions. It lets you list, view, create, and update discussions from the CLI.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Manage sub-issues, types, and dependencies from GitHub CLI
item.description:
GitHub CLI now supports managing issue types, parent/sub-issue relationships, and issue dependencies directly from the terminal. This lets you structure and track issues without using the browser.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot Chat now sees your agent sessions
item.description:
GitHub Copilot Chat on the web now has a better handoff to Copilot cloud agent sessions. It also adds the ability to search and query past agent sessions.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprises can now create up to 500 cost centers
item.description:
GitHub has doubled the enterprise cost center limit from 250 to 500. This applies to enterprises managing many business units, departments, or products.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Incremental analysis for Go, C/C++, and CodeQL CLI
item.description:
CodeQL pull request scans for C/C++ and Go now use incremental analysis, which makes them faster. GitHub says this builds on earlier incremental analysis improvements for other languages and CodeQL CLI.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Dedicated security review command now available in Copilot CLI
item.description:
GitHub Copilot CLI now includes an experimental /security-review slash command for running security reviews on code changes directly in the CLI. The feature is in public preview.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Dependabot version updates now support the Deno ecosystem
item.description:
Dependabot version updates now support Deno. The support is for version updates only, not security updates.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Upcoming breaking changes for npm v12
item.description:
npm v12 will change the default behavior of npm install with security-related defaults. The post says these changes are already available as warnings in npm 11.16.0 and newer.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Claude Fable 5 is generally available for GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Claude Fable 5 from Anthropic is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. GitHub describes it as a Mythos-class model aimed at long-horizon, autonomous coding and knowledge-work tasks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Periodic code scanning of inactive repositories
item.description:
GitHub code scanning now supports scheduled security scans for repositories with no pushes or pull requests for six months or longer. This helps organizations keep inactive repositories under periodic review.

  • Source: GitHub
